body: MQTT over TLS 1.3 -- `mqtts` -- against mosquitto's TLS listener.

author: blu
body: The client's X25519 private key and handshake random, fixed so a run is reproducible. A real client takes both from entropy.

author: blu
body: The anchor: the fixture CA the broker's leaf was minted against. Read by the harness out of the same fixture, so there is one source of truth for these bytes.

author: blu
body: The MQTT endpoint is fed out of the TLS endpoint's application buffer, not off the socket. `tls-ep-app-in` accumulates decrypted application bytes across records, so a single MQTT packet split across two TLS records reassembles here for free -- and a TLS record carrying three MQTT packets is drained by `mqtt-ep-recv` reporting what it consumed.

author: blu
body: One round: take a TLS record, decrypt it, and hand everything the application buffer now holds to the MQTT endpoint. `mr-used` tracks how much of that buffer has already been consumed, because `tls-ep-app-in` only ever grows.
